analysis: The only changed file is EngineV2BridgeTests.swift, a test-only file in provider-swift/Tests. Changes: StubTokenizer gains decodeTable (lines 146-147, 155); makeBridge gains a stopStringScope parameter (lines 440, 459); a new suite of stop-string-scope tests (lines 811-896). The tests exercise EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence with scope, ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope, ReasoningStopScope.scope, and propagation of stopStringScope into CBv2Request. The pump-receipt tests and cacheSalt tests (lines 296-432, 758-782) are unchanged and pin that caller-controlled prompt_cache_key/user do not become cache identity, which supports T-041's mitigation. No production code, trust boundaries, key handling, attestation, cache storage or network surfaces are modified in the supplied evidence. The test code contains no secrets and ships no production attack surface. The production changes the tests imply (stop-string scope in EngineV2Bridge, EngineV2Translation, ModelEOSPolicy, ReasoningStopScope) are not in this batch. Open question for integration: whether the scoped stop-string logic could affect billing or usage accounting (completion token counts, matchedStopSequence reporting), or let a consumer influence the stop behavior of reasoning spans. Those would be correctness or integrity concerns rather than confidentiality ones, and are unverifiable from test-only evidence. No threat-model assumption is invalidated by this batch.
